faq.a: Five: SIP (monthly investment growth), Lumpsum (one-time), Step-up SIP (with an annual increase percentage), SWP (systematic withdrawal from a corpus), and Goal Planner (works backward to find the monthly SIP needed to reach a target). You enter expected return per year, time period, and an inflation rate, and it shows invested, returns and maturity value.

Yes. Alongside the nominal maturity value it shows the inflation-adjusted (real) value using your inflation rate, so you can see what the corpus is actually worth in today's money. Amounts are formatted in the Indian numbering system (lakh/crore) and also written out in words.

faq.q: What detail does it give beyond the final figure?
faq.a: A year-by-year table with opening balance, amount invested, growth and closing value for each year, plus a growth chart plotting cumulative invested against total value. SIP, Step-up SIP and Lumpsum can be exported — the PDF even states the year returns overtake the amount invested. You can also compare up to three different return assumptions side by side.

No, and the tool says so clearly. Returns are assumptions for planning only, not guarantees — mutual funds carry market risk, and it advises confirming with a SEBI-registered advisor. It is not financial advice. Calculations run in your browser; your inputs are saved locally under sipCalc, and you can export a projection as PDF or CSV.
